newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Defiant Shenzhen shares end up despite crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Defiant Shenzhen shares end up despite crackdown.

text.p: Shenzhen's shares closed higher on Friday, escaping the full impact of a tough government czackdown on the market with the suspension of market heavyweight Shenzhen Development Bank, traders said.
The domestic currency A share index powered up 18.18 points or 4.40 percent to 431.09 after opening down 5.67 percent. Turnover was 7.0 billion yuan against Thursday's 4.8 billion yuan.
The foreign currency B share index gained 2.84 points or 1.98 percent to 146.16 on thin turnover of HK$54 million against Thursday's HK$73 million.
"Investors bought on the feeling that the bulk of rumoured bad news has come out," said Peter Ho, an analyst at PBI Securities (Hong Kong) in Shenzhen.

After the markets closed on Thursday, Beijing ordered the dismissal of the heads of the Shenzhen bank and three top brokerages, and banned the three securities houses from trading on their own account for one year.
Traders said the markets, especially the A share index, were rescued from a more pronounced nosedive early in the morning by the suspension of trade in Shenzhen Development Bank.
The Shenzhen Stock Exchange halted trading in the country's only domestically listed bank after Beijing announced it was being punished for illegally trading its own shares.
Earnings from the illegal share deals were confiscated, official media said. Bank officials declined to comment.
Talk of Beijing's plan to ease credit by lowering bank reserve requirements also fuelled today's rise, analysts said.
"But I do not think shares will rebound sharply next week as there are still rumours of more anti-speculation measures," an analyst at China Securities Co said.

Beijing stepped up its efforts to cool the markets last week when it ordered all state banks to unwind their stock market positions within 10 sessions to reduce the inflow of speculative funds to China's heated markets.
"Beijing has more crackdown measures on hand. It is just a matter of when it decides to put them into the market," the China Securities analyst said.

On the B share market, the big gainer was Chiwan Wharf Holdings which rose HK$0.45 or 9.18 percent to HK$5.35. The best A share issue was Yanbian Road which rose 0.90 yuan, its 10 percent limit, to 9.88 yuan.
